positions.commentary: Amazon will enter any space with its scale advantages and will not let up on competition.

thesis: This episode argues that Amazon is a superior investment compared to early-stage startups because it is growing at a significantly faster rate (40%) than other major tech companies. The speakers highlight Amazon's decentralized structure, its rational guiding principles, and its aggressive willingness to kill non-viable projects or enter any new space with scale advantages to dominate competition.

claims.claim: The speaker views Amazon as a superior investment compared to startups because it is growing faster than any of them.
claims.quote: I regularly look at Amazon stock and think, why does anyone invest in startups? Why not just invest in a trillion and a half dollar public company that's growing faster than any of them.

claims.claim: Amazon is growing at 40%, which is significantly faster than the other big five tech companies.
claims.quote: Even just looking at the big five tech companies, you look at their growth rates. Amazon's growing at 40%. None of the others are even close.

claims.claim: Amazon is decentralized, works on many different things, and operates with a guiding principle of rationality.
claims.quote: I think what's amazing about Amazon is they are so decentralized and are working on so many different things and they are, I don't know, you could almost argue that as an organization as a whole, one of their guiding principles is just rationality.

claims.claim: Amazon will kill projects that do not make sense and will compete head-to-head with any company entering their space.
claims.quote: And if things don't make sense, they'll kill it. So a really interesting thing in our top 10 acquisitions and really most of the acquisitions we've covered on the show, you very rarely see Amazon. They don't pay up for anything.
